claims.finding: MBBSEmu models RTKICK as a one-shot delayed routine whose delay is specified in seconds; MajorMUD disassembly evidence shows WCCMMUD registering background routines via RTKICK/_MY_RTKICK.
MBBSEmu documents RTIHDLR as running at 18Hz (~55ms) in the original DOS MajorBBS/Worldgroup environment. This supports hardware/host interval timing, not modem-ping timing.
MBBSEmu Galgsbl allocates TICKER and increments it once per second. This is host/GSBL timing evidence but is not itself proof of MajorMUD gameplay tick duration.

Original WCCMMUD.DOC states users may configure the maximum number of pages/global messages received in a 3 second interval. This is primary WCC documentation for at least one 3-second MajorMUD window.

Original WCCMMUD.RLN exposes INITRATE and POLLRATE as performance/polling configuration, confirming MajorMUD has internal initialization and polling rate controls; these do not directly prove 1.5s or 3.0s combat/recovery constants.

MMUD Explorer declares ROUND_SECS=5 and SPELL_ROUND_SECS=3, and comments refer to combat round 5s typical. This conflicts with the user-supplied 1.5s combat-round hypothesis and appears to represent MMUD Explorer/XP-per-hour modeling rather than direct Classic engine proof.

MMUD Explorer models stock mob HP regeneration at 18 rounds and GreaterMUD at 6 rounds. If paired with its ROUND_SECS=5 model this implies stock mob HP regen around 90s; this is a candidate calculation, not verified Classic runtime behavior.

User supplied a MegaMUD-style Timing excerpt with CommandDelay=1500, CombatPulse=1500, and TickSyncBuffer=3000. This is highly relevant but remains needs-provenance until the original file/source path is present in the repo or a MegaMUD master archive is provided.
